trusted_external_entities.name: Validator Operator
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validator operators have custody of validator keys and submit signed operations. They are authenticated via cryptographic signatures on consolidation/exit requests but their input data must still be validated (fee payment, pubkey format, queue capacity). High-value actors with stake at risk.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Chain
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The consensus layer is a separate system component maintaining validator registry and balances. While generally trusted as an authoritative source, execution layer must validate data format and handle edge cases. Cross-layer trust boundary exists.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Generic transaction submitters via RPC or P2P can be anyone. All transaction data requires comprehensive validation: type byte, signature, nonce, fee parameters, gas limits. No implicit trust - fully adversarial input.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blob Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Submitters of EIP-4844 blob transactions are untrusted external actors. All blob-specific parameters require validation: versioned hash format, blob gas limits, fee sufficiency, blob data presence, KZG commitment verification.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Validator operator has key custody but all request parameters must be validated: address format (20 bytes), pubkey format (48 bytes each), fee payment sufficient, queue not at capacity.
Exit request is signed by the validator operator. Validator index must be validated against registry. Exit processing subject to churn limiting to prevent rapid stake withdrawal attacks.

Beacon chain provides authoritative validator data, but execution layer must validate format and apply protocol rules (min balance check, effective balance cap at 2048 ETH, compounding prefix verification).

Raw transaction bytes from untrusted source. Must validate: transaction type byte recognition (0x00-0x03), RLP deserialization, signature verification, all fee constraints, contract creation eligibility.

Blob transactions require comprehensive validation: blob gas within protocol limits, blob fee meets base fee, versioned hash format valid (0x01 prefix, 32 bytes), blob data present and matches commitments.

Raw blob data for KZG commitment generation. Blob must be properly formatted. Versioned hash creation adds version byte prefix. Attackers cannot forge valid versioned hashes without possessing corresponding blob data.
